aPlutoTeam v103.3 trajectory findings
=======================================

Dataset
-------
Generation 1: 2,192 recorded model steps, final frame 20,207,
~295.7 MB trajectory payload.

Key finding: owner rewrite drift, not merely untrained ally embedding
--------------------------------------------------------------------
The v103.3 matcher used live raw SCR CUnits. By late game, moving-unit
x/y/order drift caused many observation rows to fail matching.

Across all 2,192 steps:
- only ~20.0% of steps had unmatched=0
- median unmatched rows: 16
- maximum unmatched rows: 66
- median unmatched rate among non-self player rows: ~18.5%
- maximum unmatched rate: ~47.8%

Unmatched non-self rows were defaulted to ENEMY.

The periodic live relation logs and rewritten model input prove the effect:
enemy over-count is extremely correlated with unmatched rows (r ≈ 0.974).

Concrete suspicious ally-base episode
-------------------------------------
At model step frame 17,928:
- Pluto action: a=6 AttackMove
- selected own units: 13
- decoded destination: (3280, 2992)
- destination is directly inside the 5-o'clock Zerg ally cluster
- rewritten model view within 256 px of target: 18 ally, 5 enemy
- unmatched rows in that step: 38

At model step frame 19,337:
- Pluto action: a=6 AttackMove
- selected own units: 7
- decoded destination: (3856, 2576)
- rewritten view within 256 px: 17 ally, 3 enemy
- unmatched rows: 58

Around those frames the live relation logger reported only roughly 9-22
actually visible enemies globally, while the rewritten model request often
contained 40-60+ enemy rows. The excess tracks unmatched rows.

Conclusion
----------
Do NOT train ally embedding from this v103.3 dataset yet. Relation labels are
too contaminated late game. First fix owner row matching, recollect a clean
trajectory, and require late-game unmatched to remain near zero.

v104 implements that compatibility fix by matching against the coherent
g_legacyCUnits[] shadow that original Pluto observed for the same snapshot.
